take: the boring database finally learned how to save your ass
tldr: Snapshots exist now. Real ones: online, point-in-time, restorable without a support ticket. That was the dealbreaker in our last verdict and it is gone. The rest is one config rename, one protocol cut, and a health check with opinions.

highlights.name: Point-in-time snapshots
highlights.what: acmedb snapshot create takes a consistent snapshot without pausing writes, and restore replays the WAL to any second inside the retention window. This is the feature we yelled about. It is real.

highlights.name: Manifest compaction
highlights.what: The manifest no longer grows forever, so cold starts on old databases drop from minutes to seconds. Nobody will tweet about it. Everybody will feel it.

highlights.name: acmedb doctor
highlights.what: A health check that tells you what is wrong in plain English instead of a hex dump. Petty? Yes. Useful? Also yes.

bottom_line: This is the release that moves AcmeDB from cute toy to fine for prod, behind a cache. Upgrade, take a snapshot, go to bed.

sources.quote: Snapshots are online, incremental, and restorable to any point in the last seven days.
Cold start on a 500 GB database fell from 4 minutes to 9 seconds.
Snapshots of databases over 2 TB take hours, not minutes.
Still single-region. Cross-region replication is on the roadmap.
